structural_validity_gate.claim: Binary hard-usability gate for text units that are decodable, non-corrupted, and structurally usable for language-model training.
structural_validity_gate.formal_definition: Pass/fail gate over hard structural invalidity only: empty or too-short units, encoding/control-character corruption, non-language fragments, excessive symbol noise, markup/extraction residue, and broken repetition runs. The gate records decision_scope=structural_usability_only and explicitly excludes semantic quality, duplicate status, coverage balance, and Utility outcomes.
expected_behavior: Passes readable prose, structured lists, instructional text, and technical-reference text when they are decodable and structurally usable.
Rejects corrupted, markup-residue-heavy, symbol-noisy, empty, or broken-repetition text units.
failure_modes: May still reject very short snippets that are readable but below the minimum learnable-unit threshold.
Does not protect against low information value; observable selection-value evidence may inform optional Stage-B budget allocation.
acceptance_tests: structural_validity_gate(clean_structured) > structural_validity_gate(noisy_corrupted)
style-repetitive but readable educational/reference text remains valid and is reported through warning_rules, not violated_rules
structural_validity_gate records decision_scope=structural_usability_only
warning_rules may be present on valid chunks and do not fail the gate

structural_validity_score.claim: Soft support score and audit surface for the hard Validity gate; it is not a standalone quality or selection objective.
structural_validity_score.formal_definition: Continuous diagnostic score based only on structural usability features. Hard failures are listed in violated_rules; style or borderline concerns are listed in warning_rules and do not invalidate a chunk by themselves. This score is an audit surface for the binary gate, not a ranking objective.
expected_behavior: Higher on clean structured prose than malformed/noisy fragments.
Readable repetitive educational/reference text may receive warnings without failing the gate.
failure_modes: Can under-score short but valid snippets.
Should not be interpreted as information quality.
acceptance_tests: structural_validity_score(clean_structured) > structural_validity_score(noisy_corrupted)
warning_rules are diagnostic and do not directly determine pass/fail
structural_validity_score exposes hard_rule_count and warning_rule_count
structural_validity_score excludes reference_quality_score and duplicate indicators from its decision

reference_quality_score.claim: Frozen pre-outcome selection-value proxy for observable information density, structural usefulness, and boilerplate risk; not intrinsic data quality.
reference_quality_score.formal_definition: Legacy metric name for a reference-trained pre-outcome selection-value proxy. It estimates observable information density, coherence-like structure, and useful content support for chunks that already pass Validity, while penalizing boilerplate and low-information patterns. It is a Stage-B selection signal, not a hard gate, not intrinsic ground-truth quality, and not a Utility outcome. The canonical score is style_length_normalized_quality_v2: raw reference-model evidence is calibrated by validity hygiene, information support, lexical diversity, style bucket, and length bucket so short informative, instructional, structured-list, and technical-reference chunks are not penalized solely by prose/length bias, while boilerplate and low-information text remain low selection-value. The selector applies a soft top-tail anti-collapse policy: it measures fine-grained high proxy-score bands and caps excessive q>=0.99 concentration with a bounded swap ratio, rather than forcing exact quality-band distribution matching.
expected_behavior: Higher on informative coherent chunks than shallow procedural, boilerplate, or corrupted-readable text.
Does not replace Validity; clean but low-information chunks may remain valid while receiving low Quality.
Does not certify true data quality or training usefulness; Stage C must validate downstream effect.
Short informative or technical-reference chunks can remain competitive when structural hygiene, information support, and lexical diversity are present.
failure_modes: Reference-model domain shift can still affect calibration.
Style/length calibration reduces systematic bias but does not certify learning utility.
acceptance_tests: reference_quality_score(explanatory) > reference_quality_score(shallow_procedural)
reference_quality_score(coherent_prose) > reference_quality_score(corrupted_readable)
reference_quality_score(informative_dense) > reference_quality_score(template_boilerplate)
reference_quality_score(clean_structured) > reference_quality_score(template_boilerplate)
quality audit reports by_style_bucket, by_domain_bucket_top, by_length_bucket, and valid_but_low_quality
reference_quality_score is used in Stage-B selection and not as a Stage-A hard gate
reference_quality_score details declare canonical_core_axis=Selection Value Evidence and hard_reject_authority=false

when no training budget is constrained, Stage B may emit retain_all

exact_duplicate_indicator.claim: Detect exact duplicates from text hash collisions.
exact_duplicate_indicator.formal_definition: Binary duplicate indicator from corpus hash counts.
expected_behavior: 1 for exact duplicates and 0 otherwise.
failure_modes: Cannot detect paraphrased near duplicates.
acceptance_tests: exact_duplicate_indicator(exact_duplicate) > exact_duplicate_indicator(clean_structured)

shingle_near_duplicate_indicator.claim: Binary fuzzy near-duplicate evidence from locality-sensitive shortlist plus overlap verification.
shingle_near_duplicate_indicator.formal_definition: Binary fuzzy near-duplicate evidence using local simhash buckets and verified shingle overlap thresholds. Independent holdout precision and useful-data-dropout gates are not satisfied, so this signal cannot authorize irreversible Stage-A rejection.
expected_behavior: Higher on repeated template variants than unique prose.
failure_modes: Low lexical-overlap paraphrases may pass.
acceptance_tests: shingle_near_duplicate_indicator(near_duplicate) > shingle_near_duplicate_indicator(clean_structured)

shingle_near_duplicate_risk_score.claim: Continuous harmful-redundancy risk used as a Stage B redundancy penalty while preserving useful recurrence.
shingle_near_duplicate_risk_score.formal_definition: Continuous risk from verified overlap, SimHash prefix pressure, and intra-chunk repetition pressure. The canonical risk is harmful_redundancy_minus_useful_recurrence_v1: exact/near duplicate burden remains penalized, but definitional, example-driven, exercise-like, and technical-reference recurrence receives limited relief when verified overlap is low. This keeps Redundancy focused on wasteful repetition rather than all repeated pedagogical or reference structure.
expected_behavior: Higher on near-duplicate or copied chunks than clean unique chunks.
Higher on wasteful repeated fragments than on structured definitions, examples, exercises, or technical-reference recurrence with low verified overlap.
failure_modes: Can still under-detect semantic paraphrase duplicates.
Useful-recurrence relief is conservative and requires broader benchmark calibration.
acceptance_tests: near_dup(near_duplicate) > near_dup(clean_structured)
shingle_near_duplicate_risk_score(intra_chunk_repetitive) > shingle_near_duplicate_risk_score(clean_structured)
shingle_near_duplicate_risk_score details include redundancy_policy=harmful_redundancy_minus_useful_recurrence_v1
shingle_near_duplicate_risk_score details include harmful_redundancy_risk and useful_recurrence_score

allowed_signals: local text-structure markers only to distinguish useful recurrence from harmful redundancy

subset_coverage_retention_score.claim: Evaluate subset coverage preservation, especially tail-cluster retention.
subset_coverage_retention_score.formal_definition: Subset-level composite of distribution similarity, rare-cluster retention ratio, retained rare-cluster count, and declared domain/capability-mix drift when metadata and a Deployment Contract support that axis. Coverage is reported as source coverage, style coverage, semantic cluster-backbone coverage, and observed composition drift. Domain coverage is only claimed when explicit domain metadata exists; target-mix satisfaction is only claimed when a target mix is declared and validated. Otherwise source buckets and observed domain arms are reported as fallback/diagnostic support and must not be over-claimed as semantic web-domain coverage or a universal domain ratio. A diagnostic learning-signal coverage report compares the selected subset against the canonical multi-matched Stage-A baseline for token novelty, phrase novelty, concept density, moderate difficulty share, and template density. This report is diagnostic only and does not replace Utility outcome validation.
expected_behavior: Selected subsets retain head/tail semantic clusters rather than only high-quality head clusters.
Selected subsets preserve source/style bucket distributions when those supports are enforced.
Certification distinguishes source fallback from explicit domain metadata and reports semantic backbone readiness separately.
Reports selected-vs-baseline learning-signal gaps without using them as Utility pass/fail evidence.
failure_modes: Depends on upstream cluster quality.
Domain retention is only as explicit as the available metadata or source fallback buckets.
acceptance_tests: subset_coverage_retention_score(selected_subset) is reported together with distribution_similarity, tail_cluster_retention, tail_cluster_retained_count, source_coverage_support, domain_coverage_support, style_coverage_support, and semantic_coverage_support
subset_coverage_retention_score is only treated as passing when cluster_backbone_audit.passed == true in certification mode
domain_coverage_support records support_scope so fallback source buckets are not over-claimed as explicit domain metadata
style_coverage_support, source/domain bucket support, and semantic_coverage_support are validated separately from the scalar coverage score
coverage_axis_components reports source, style, and semantic support payloads
coverage_details include learning_signal_coverage_diagnostic with selected, baseline, gaps_selected_minus_baseline, and risk_flags
learning_signal_coverage_diagnostic policy is diagnostic_only_not_selector_objective

allowed_signals: explicit domain metadata distribution support when available

small_lm_probe_gain_score.claim: Measure Utility as a control-validated small-LM evidence protocol that separates probe sensitivity, selected-over-random curation benefit, and selected-over-multi-matched strict counterfactual benefit.
small_lm_probe_gain_score.formal_definition: Utility is a Stage-C subset-level validation protocol rather than a selector objective. The protocol first runs a small-LM sensitivity audit with a common Stage-A baseline disjoint from all sensitivity arms. Destructive probe validity requires positive_control > baseline_stageA_random > corrupted_negative_control, where corrupted_negative_control destroys next-token structure with hash-noise text. Control ordering also reports MDE-aware margins so near-noise differences are treated as inconclusive rather than decisive failures. A separate token_shuffle_negative_control is reported as token-inventory stress; decisive failure there is token-exposure confounding, while below-MDE failure is a token-exposure inconclusive caveat, not the destructive sanity check itself. Same-dataset low-quality controls are retained as diagnostics because they can still improve NLL through vocabulary and domain-token exposure. The protocol then reports curation benefit as selected versus baseline_stageA_random under equal token budgets, and reports strict counterfactual benefit as selected versus baseline_multi_matched_stageA_random, where the multi-matched baseline is sampled from Stage-A records matched by quality band, length bucket, style bucket, and domain bucket with hierarchical fallback. In-domain and all-pairwise OOD cells are evaluated with paired held-out documents, delta-NLL, paired-bootstrap CI lower bound, minimum detectable effect, seed/bucket stability, and train-exposure audit fields. The canonical Stage-C strict pass remains tied to baseline_multi_matched_stageA_random, but reporting no longer collapses all Utility failures into one negative score: aggregate evidence reports probe_sensitivity_status, curation_benefit_status, strict_counterfactual_status, utility_probe_valid, utility_strict_pass, failure_reason, and evidence_tier. Evidence tiers include not_evaluable_utility_evidence, probe_valid_token_exposure_caveat, random_baseline_gain, random_baseline_gain_with_token_exposure_caveat, matched_baseline_inconclusive, matched_baseline_gain, and strict_certification_ready. baseline_stageA_random is the curation-benefit baseline; baseline_multi_matched_stageA_random is the strict counterfactual certification baseline; quality-, length-, style-, and full-random baselines remain diagnostic stress tests.
small_lm_probe_gain_score.expected_behavior: A valid Utility result first shows probe sensitivity on controls, then indicates whether selected beats Stage-A random, and only claims strict certification when selected beats the multi-matched Stage-A baseline under the configured CI/MDE/strict-min policy.
failure_modes: Probe sensitivity can be not evaluable for a dataset if positive/random/destructive-negative controls are not ordered; this is reported as not_evaluable_utility_evidence rather than selector failure.
Token-shuffle stress can expose token-inventory confounding even when the destructive sanity check passes; this is reported as a token-exposure caveat.
Selected subsets may beat Stage-A random while remaining inconclusive or negative against the multi-matched counterfactual; this is curation evidence but not strict certification.
Small eval slices, weak probe capacity, or small effect sizes can make CI/MDE evidence inconclusive even when mean deltas are positive.
Strict all-pairwise OOD certification can fail even when in-domain Utility is positive, indicating transfer limitation rather than upstream metric failure.
acceptance_tests: small_lm_probe_gain_score(selected_subset) > 0 against baseline_multi_matched_stageA_random on required eval cells

fixed_token_probe_gain_score.claim: Deprecated compatibility alias for the old hybrid n-gram utility probe.
fixed_token_probe_gain_score.formal_definition: Legacy utility output retained for compatibility only; not canonical for Stage C utility decisions.
expected_behavior: Matches the corresponding small LM score only as a compatibility alias.
failure_modes: Must not be treated as the canonical utility validator.
acceptance_tests: fixed_token_probe_gain_score is retained only as a deprecated compatibility diagnostic and is not used for canonical utility pass/fail

explanatory_quality_proxy.formal_definition: Heuristic/prototype similarity based explanatory-style estimate for diagnostics.
expected_behavior: Higher on explanation-heavy text than shallow procedural text.
failure_modes: Heuristic penalties can overfit style artifacts.
acceptance_tests: explanatory_quality_proxy(explanatory) > explanatory_quality_proxy(shallow_procedural)

tail_cluster_rarity_proxy.claim: Diagnostic proxy for chunk rarity in cluster space.
tail_cluster_rarity_proxy.formal_definition: Cluster-size-based rarity estimate at chunk level.
expected_behavior: Higher for smaller/rarer clusters.
failure_modes: Can overrate rare but low-value clusters.
acceptance_tests: tail_cluster_rarity_proxy(tail_rare) > tail_cluster_rarity_proxy(head_common)

predictive_utility_proxy.claim: Diagnostic utility surrogate for comparison only.
predictive_utility_proxy.formal_definition: Diagnostic utility surrogate for development inspection only. It is explicitly excluded from canonical selector objectives, Stage-C Utility pass/fail, and certification readiness.
expected_behavior: May correlate with utility outcome but must not drive canonical selection or validation.
failure_modes: Can remain heuristic-only and diverge from actual LM utility.
acceptance_tests: predictive_utility_proxy(explanatory) > predictive_utility_proxy(shallow_procedural)
predictive_utility_proxy is diagnostic and absent from selector objective weights
predictive_utility_proxy is not used for Stage-C Utility pass/fail

buckets.coherent_prose: Natural coherent prose with low procedural noise.
buckets.corrupted_readable: Readable but degraded text with corruption or high repetition artifacts.
buckets.informative_dense: Information-dense content with strong concept or explanatory support.
buckets.template_boilerplate: Template-heavy, boilerplate, or procedural filler text.
buckets.non_prose_structured: Structured instructional, technical-reference, or list-like text.
buckets.intra_chunk_repetitive: Non-duplicate chunks with excessive internal repetition.
